title: Himalayan North
desc: Mountainous and beautiful, a tourist destination for the adventurous and the spiritual. This region contains some of India's most visited hill stations and religious places.

title: Plains (India)
desc: The plains, India's breadbasket, are watered by the holy rivers Ganges and Yamuna and their tributaries. The region also features the country's capital New Delhi, Agra of Taj Mahal fame, and the holy cities of Mathura, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Bodh Gaya and Amritsar. Many of the events that shaped India's history took place in this region.

title: Western India
desc: Home to the vast Thar Desert; the colourful palaces, forts and cities of Rajasthan; the country's most vibrant and biggest city, Mumbai; the mesmerising rock-cut caves of Ajanta and Ellora in Maharashtra; pristine forests; the wonderful beaches of Goa; the Asiatic lions of Gujarat in Gir jungles; and the rapidly developing cities of Ahmedabad, Surat, Jaipur and Pune.

title: Central India
desc: Breathtaking and vibrant, a landlocked region that offers everything from rolling hills, dramatic waterfalls and abundant wildlife, to classical architecture, tribal heritage and modern steel industry. Home to the Vindhya and Satpura mountains; the Chitrakote Falls; the prehistoric Bhimbetka caves; the erotic sculptures of Khajuraho; and the Bhilai-Durg industrial area.

title: Eastern India
desc: Economically less developed, but culturally rich and perhaps the most welcoming to outsiders. Features Kolkata, once the capital of British India, and the temple cities of Puri, Bhubaneswar and Konark. The region stretches from the mountains to the coast, resulting in fascinating variations in climate. It is also the mineral storehouse of India, having the country's largest and richest mines.

title: North-Eastern India
desc: Insular and relatively virgin, this is the country's tribal corner, with lush, beautiful landscapes, endemic flora and fauna of the Indo-Malayan group and famed tea gardens. Consists of seven states popularly known as the "Seven Sisters". The world's oldest polo ground, the world's only floating national park, the world's only women-run market and the world's tallest topiary plant can be seen in Manipur. The state of Meghalaya is depicted as the "Scotland of India" because of its mesmerising environment.

title: Southern India
desc: Features famous and historical temples, tropical forests, backwaters, beaches, hill stations, and three big cities of Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and other smaller cities. The city of Mysore is world-renowned for its palaces, especially the Mysore Palace. The island groups of Andaman and Nicobar on the east and Lakshadweep on the west, included in this region for convenience, are far from the mainland and have their unique characteristics, known for beautiful beaches and an off the beaten path tourist getaway.

title: Bengaluru/West Central
desc: Contains the original mud fort, the old neighbourhoods and the western fringes of the British-era Cantonment.

title: Bengaluru/East Central
desc: The eastern parts of the Cantonment, a popular spot for shopping and dining.

title: Bengaluru/North
desc: The northern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to many gated communities. The Aero India show is hosted here at Yelahanka Air Force Base.

title: Bengaluru/South
desc: The southern suburbs of Bengaluru, home to many cafés, lakes and India's IT and biotech mecca of Electronic City.

title: Bengaluru/East
desc: The eastern suburbs of Bengaluru, the centre of the city's booming IT industry.

title: Chennai/North
desc: The oldest part of the city north of the Coovum River. Home to MGR Chennai Central and Chennai Port.

title: Chennai/Central
desc: The modern city centre between Coovum and Adyar rivers. Home to Santhome Church, Marina Beach and the Tamil film industry Kollywood.

title: Chennai/South
desc: The newer part of the city south of the Adyar River. Home to Chennai Airport.

title: Hyderabad/West
desc: Hyderabad's premier technology hub with offices of Microsoft, Oracle, Infosys, and many other IT and BPO (business process outsourcing) firms. Home to cosmopolitan crows, hip restaurants and bars, and attractions like Shilparamam, Botanical Garden, Durgam Cheruvu and the Osman Sagar.

title: Hyderabad/East
desc: The well-developed industrial suburbs at the east, with pharmaceutical factories and middle-class housing. Other than the occasional park and the odd restaurant, it is most visited for the resorts on the outskirts of the city, as well as Ramoji Film City.

title: Hyderabad/South
desc: The southern suburbs of Hyderabad. Home to the Nehru Zoological Park, the Himayat Sagar and the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport.

title: Kolkata/BBD Bagh
desc: The colonial district is still the city's central administrative district, with one of the best remnants of British colonial architecture in the world.

title: Kolkata/Esplanade
desc: The modern heart of Kolkata, and the city's central business district.

title: Kolkata/Maidan
desc: A urban space with numerous festivals, sports, rallies and protests.

title: Kolkata/South
desc: The posh and new part of the city.

title: Kolkata/Southern Suburbs
desc: The rapidly mushrooming localities to the south of the city. This is a relatively newer part of the city where a lot of expansion is going on.

title: Kolkata/North
desc: The older area of the city, a fascinating district dominated by narrow little lanes and hundreds of century-old buildings. North Kolkata was known as Black Town during the British period as it was home to the native population.

title: Kolkata/Northern Suburbs
desc: The large industrial area to the north of the city with a number of factories, including jute, paper, cotton, ordnance and chemicals. Also a major transport hub in the city where air travel and rapid transit converge.

title: Kolkata/East
desc: Rapidly developing, especially the IT and finance sectors. Home to many shopping malls, five-star hotels, theme parks, posh housing estates and technology parks.

title: Mumbai/Western Suburbs
desc: Home to those who want to have a more peaceful surrounding. It has a few beaches and promenades. Home to a large Christian community and the city's most famous church.

title: Mumbai/Eastern Suburbs
desc: A middle-class bastion. Mulund and Ghatkopar are home to a predominantly middle and upper-middle-class populace, many from the entrepreneurial Gujarati community.

title: Mumbai/North
desc: Has some beaches that are not dirty. Other than this, it is just another victim of Mumbai's vast urban sprawl. Contains Mumbai's oldest heritage sites, as well as the "Film City" that defined Bollywood.

title: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
desc: The lungs of Mumbai; famous for its leopards and the caves inside the park.

title: Jammu and Kashmir
desc: With its mountains and lakes, this is a popular destination with travellers, although the conflict escalation between Pakistan and India has decreased its popularity.

title: Ladakh
desc: Ladakh was an independent kingdom for centuries and still with its own vibrant culture. Offering much in the way of sightseeing, backpacking and trekking it's not to be missed.

title: Himachal Pradesh
desc: A pleasant, laid back, predominantly Hindu state, with a Tibetan refugee population; popular with tourists.

title: Uttarakhand
desc: The source of the holy Ganges and Yamuna, it has a number of pilgrimage sites, earning the nichname 'Devbhoomi', literally 'the Land of the Gods'.

title: Punjab (India)
desc: Named for the five rivers that flow through the region, Punjab is India's breadbasket. The majority-Sikh state is home to that faith's holiest site – the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

title: Haryana
desc: Carved out of Punjab in the 1960s, Haryana is home to Gurugram (Gurgaon), the beating heart of India's information technology and automotive industries.

title: Uttar Pradesh
desc: The most populous state in both India and the world with its wide range of attractions, from the world-famous Taj Mahal to the ancient city of Varanasi.

title: Bihar
desc: Home to the birthplace of Buddhism, the world's oldest residential university, and the heartland of the Maurya Empire, India's poorest state has made considerable economic strides in the 2020s.

title: Rajasthan
desc: The land of warriors, deserts, colourful saris, historic forts and Rajput temples

title: Gujarat
desc: Home to Asiatic lions and fine textiles, developing fast especially around Ahmedabad and Surat

title: Maharashtra
desc: India's richest state by GDP, home to cities like Mumbai, Pune, Aurangabad and Nagpur.

title: Goa
desc: Home to the country's best beaches and commonly known as the "party state". Former Portuguese colony.

title: Chhattisgarh
desc: Forests abound in wildlife, breathtaking waterfalls and fascinating tribal culture.

title: Madhya Pradesh
desc: India's second-largest state by area, home to the Bhimbetka caves and the famous erotic temples at Khajuraho.

title: Jharkhand
desc: A contrast with some of the oldest cave paintings in India and some of the fastest industrialising cities.

title: Odisha
desc: You can discover the religious sites or enjoy some time at the beach in this state.

title: Sikkim
desc: Experience the natural beauty of the Himalayas with its valleys, forests and waterfalls.

title: West Bengal
desc: A state with some of the marvellous landscape features and cultural heritage.

title: Arunachal Pradesh
desc: An ethnically diverse state, home to several tribal groups and a large Tibetan Buddhist following. Administered by India but also claimed by China (as South Tibet).

title: Assam
desc: Known worldwide for Assam tea and being the first site for oil production in Asia. Also home to some national parks, some of which are designated as World Heritage Sites.

title: Manipur
desc: Credited for introducing the sport of polo to Europeans, Manipur is known as the "Jewel of India", with its capital city as the "Flower on Lofty Heights". The state's also contains the world's only floating national park.

title: Meghalaya
desc: Known for having a capital that is often dubbed as the "Scotland of the East" and amazing, jubilant scenery. The state is one of the few Christian-majority states in India.

title: Mizoram
desc: One of the most geographically isolated states in India, as well as being home to several tribes who have their roots in Southeast Asia. The state is one of the few Christian-majority states in India.

title: Nagaland
desc: Home to 16 major tribes, the state has the distinction of being one of the few Christian-majority states in India.

title: Tripura
desc: One of the most isolated Indian states, with its residents being a mix of native Tripuris as well as the ethnic Bengalis who fled from Bangladesh during the second Indo-Pakistani War.

title: Andhra Pradesh
desc: Coastal state with fiery food.

title: Telangana
desc: Known for its cultural heritage under the Nizam of Hyderabad.

title: Kerala
desc: "God's own country", famous for spices, backwaters, Ayurveda and the Malabar coast.

title: Tamil Nadu
desc: India's southern tip, famous for its temples, hills and its megacity Chennai.

title: Karnataka
desc: Kannada homeland, with India's IT capital Bengaluru and numerous off-beat destinations.

title: Jammu Division
desc: Known for its temples, shrines, palaces and forts.

title: Kashmir Valley
desc: Some say it is the Paradise on Earth, friendly people, beautiful gardens, vast lakes and pristine streams and stunning landscapes.

title: Garhwal
desc: The western and more easily accessed part famous for its religious destinations like Char Dham, Panch Prayag, Panch Kedar, Sapt Badri and Haridwar-Rishikesh.

title: Kumaon
desc: The eastern part famous for its beauty, lakes and hill stations like Nainital, Ranikhet, Kausani, Chaukori and Munsyari.

title: Doaba
desc: The area between Beas and the Sutlej rivers.

title: Majha
desc: The border area with Pakistan and the birthplace of Sikhism, home to the Golden Temple.

title: Malwa (Punjab)
desc: The southern part of the state.

title: North Haryana
desc: Fertile, high rainfall area, with agriculture and educational hubs.

title: South Haryana
desc: Semi-arid, rocky terrain with growing urbanization and massive industrial hubs due to its proximity to Delhi.

title: West Haryana
desc: Dry sandy plains bordering the Thal desert, with rural agriculture

title: Upper Doab
desc: The northwestern part of the state, covering the eastern part of the National Capital Region (NCR).

title: Braj
desc: Between the Ganges and Yamuna rivers, in the southwestern part of the state. It is home to Agra, the city of the Taj Mahal, as well as the twin pilgrimage sites of Mathura and Vrindavan.

title: Rohilkhand
desc: On the upper Ganges alluvial plain, in the northern part of the state.

title: Awadh
desc: The central part of the state including the capital, Lucknow, is known as the granary of India, and the centre of various period films of Bollywood and modern films.

title: Lower Doab
desc: The southern part of the state. Home to Kanpur and Prayagraj.

title: Purvanchal
desc: The eastern end of Uttar Pradesh, one of the most ancient regions of India, enjoying a rich heritage and culture.

title: Northern Bundelkhand
desc: A geographic and cultural region of gentle hills in the southwestern part of the state. Home to Jhansi, the city of Rani Lakshmibai, as well as the pilgrimage site of Chitrakoot.

title: Bhojpur (region)
desc: Home to ancient forts, temples, and a wildlife preserve with tigers

title: Magadha
desc: Home to Patna, once the capital of the Maurya Empire, and several historic and cultural sites.

title: Mithila
desc: A flat and fertile plain criss-crossed by numerous rivers that originate from the Himalayas.

title: Ahmedabad/Central Zone
desc: This zone mostly consists of the Walled City areas of Ahmedabad and the famous Mughal architecture of the old times. Asarva is well known for the Ahmedabad Civil Hospital.

title: Ahmedabad/North Zone
desc: Naroda is the industrial area now developing rapidly.

title: Ahmedabad/South Zone
desc: Kankariya Lake is a very popular and relaxing place here. Maninagar Railway Station serves this region of the city, as an alternative station to the main railway station in Kalupur in Central Zone. The prestigious Ahmedabad - Vadodara National Expressway - 1 starts from the C.T.M.

title: Ahmedabad/East Zone
desc: Mostly industrial areas.

title: Ahmedabad/West Zone
desc: Motera, Chandkheda and Vasna are rapidly developing suburbs. Motera-Chandkheda, in Northern portion, serve as exits to the capital and twin city of Gandhinagar via Visat-Gandhinagar Intercity Highway (up to Infocity Gandhinagar). Sabarmati is one of the oldest areas of Ahmedabad, having the Sabarmati Railway Station (SBI) for North India-bound trains (as an alternative station to the main railway station (ADI) in Kalupur in Central Zone). Ashram Road and C G Road are core business and commercial areas. Vasna is quite in Southern portion and is an industrial area.

title: Ahmedabad/New West Zone
desc: Most of them are developing suburbs. IIM-Ahmedabad, one of the best business schools in India, is in Vastrapur. Vastrapur Lake is newly built artificial lake. Ranip is close to Sabarmati and has the Sabarmati Railway Station (SBT) for trains to/from Central India (as an alternative station to the main railway station (ADI) in Kalupur in Central Zone). Bodakdev and Vastrapur are well-known for commercial centres. Sarkhej is the Ahmedabad end of SG Highway that connects to Gandhinagar on the Western side.

title: Ajmer
desc: File:Dargah Sharif Ajmer 2014-06-04 23-25.jpg Tomb of Sufi sain Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti (Pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Muslims)

title: Bharatpur
desc: Location of a famous bird sanctuary Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.

title: Bikaner
desc: File:Bikaner fort view 08.jpg Site of Bikaner fort and the area famous for its sweets.

title: Chittorgarh
desc: File:Padmini_Palace,_Chittorgarh,_Rajasthan.jpg Site of multiple battles by Maharana Pratap against Mughal emporor Akbar.

title: Jaisalmer
desc: File:Jaisalmer_Sand_Dunes.jpg The Golden City, noted for its Havelis and Thar desert Safaris.

title: Kota
desc: File:JagMandir.jpg Home to Darrah Wildlife Sanctuary, various temples and parks.

title: Udaipur
desc: File:Udaipur_palace_night.jpg Known as the City of Lakes.

title: Ajmer Division
desc: In the central part of the state, home to the Brahma temple in the holy city of Pushkar.

title: Bharatpur Division
desc: In the far eastern part of the state, home to Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary.

title: Bikaner Division
desc: In the northern part of the state, famous for its sweets.

title: Jaipur Division
desc: in the eastern part of the state, home to the state capital, Jaipur (the Pink City)

title: Jodhpur Division
desc: in the western part of the state, home to the desert near Jaisalmer (the Golden City) as well as Jodhpur (The Blue City)

title: Kota Division
desc: In the southeastern part of the state, less arid than the other divisions.

title: Udaipur Division
desc: In the southern part of the state, home to Udaipur and all its lakes and palaces.

title: North Gujarat
desc: A semi-arid to arid region with culture and language influenced by neighbouring Rajasthan

title: Central Gujarat
desc: The Gujarati heartland. Ahmedabad and Vadodara are the main cities in this region.

title: South Gujarat
desc: Hot, wet and green, this region is rapidly urbanising and industrialising

title: Saurashtra
desc: This hilly and fertile region was never part of British India. Instead it survived as more than 200 princely states under British suzeranity till independence.

title: North Konkan
desc: A scenic coastal region in western Maharashtra known for its lush greenery, pristine beaches, vibrant seafood traditions, and a rich cultural blend shaped by centuries of maritime history and diverse communities.

title: Raigad (district)
desc: a historically rich coastal district in known for its majestic forts, lush green landscapes, vibrant Konkani culture, and a strong connection to Maratha heritage, making it one of the state’s most significant and scenic regions.

title: South Konkan
desc: South Konkan is a picturesque coastal region in Maharashtra known for its serene beaches, dense coconut groves, rich seafood traditions, and a deeply rooted Konkani culture shaped by centuries of maritime history and natural beauty.

title: North Maharashtra
desc: Known for its rugged landscapes, rich agricultural heritage, and strong cultural identity, blending historic cities, fertile river valleys, and vibrant traditions into a distinct and lively part of the state.

title: Central Maharashtra
desc: A dynamic region known for its blend of rich history, vibrant cultural life, and modern educational and technological hubs.

title: South Maharashtra
desc: A culturally rich and geographically diverse region known for its fertile farmlands, historic cities, vibrant traditions, and a strong blend of coastal and inland influences.

title: Marathwada
desc: Known for its rich cultural heritage, ancient monuments, and strong agrarian traditions, blending vibrant festivals, traditional arts, and resilient communities. Home to Ajanta and Ellora Caves.

title: Vidarbha
desc: Known for its vast forests, rich wildlife, fertile plains, and a cultural identity shaped by both rural traditions and historic cities. Many people consider it to be a part of Central India rather than Western India.

title: North Goa
desc: The north is renowned for its vibrant nightlife, bustling markets, and energetic atmosphere. Popular beaches in the north, such as Baga, Calangute, and Anjuna, draw in crowds of party goers, adventurous travelers, and water sports enthusiasts. These bustling beaches are popular destination for water sport activities during the day, and as the sun sets, they become vibrant hubs of nightlife.

title: South Goa
desc: The south offers a more tranquil and peaceful atmosphere, and is a more ideal choice for travelers looking for a relaxed vacation away from the crowds. Beaches like Palolem, Agonda, and Neolem are known for their pristine white sands, crystal-clear waters, and picturesque surroundings. Here, visitors can unwind, soak up the sun, and enjoy the tranquility of the beach in a more laid-back environment.

title: North Chhattisgarh
desc: A cooler hill region known for history, temples, and Tibetan settlements such as Mainpat

title: South Chhattisgarh
desc: Densely forested tribal area with waterfalls, caves, and indigenous culture.

title: Central Madhya Pradesh
desc: Home to UNESCO heritage sites and the state capital

title: Eastern Madhya Pradesh
desc: Full of wildlife and nature

title: Narmada Valley
desc: Hill stations and rivers

title: North Coast (Odisha)
desc: Fertile land, fishing, ports, and sandy beaches

title: South Coast (Odisha)
desc: The most visited region of Odisha, home to the capital Bhubaneswar, Chilika Lake, Jagannath Temple, Konark Sun Temple and picturesque beaches.

title: Northwest Odisha
desc: Rolling hills, mining and industry

title: South Odisha
desc: The Eastern Ghats, dense forests, indigenous tribes, and hill stations

title: East Sikkim
desc: Despite being the most populated area, it has many monasteries, lakes and hidden picturesque treasures.

title: North Sikkim
desc: Even more mountainous than the rest of the state. The scenic Yumthang valley and the pretty Gurudongmar lake are some of its attractions. Entry restrictions are higher and travel is tougher here.

title: South Sikkim
desc: Warmer and has fewer mountains.

title: West Sikkim
desc: The region borders Nepal and is a great place for trekking. Pelling, in this region, has monuments of historic significance.

title: Ajodhya Hill and Forest Reserve Area
North Bengal
desc: The northern part of West Bengal with its mountains, a wide range of animals and forests, and the presence of Gorkha, Rajbanshi and tribal cultures.

title: Central Bengal
desc: The transition zone between North Bengal and South Bengal.

title: South Bengal
desc: Economic, administrative and cultural hub, stepped into history with diverse architectures, biodiversity, and once-thriving industry.

title: Southwest Bengal
desc: Less-developed region; home to beaches, forests, folk culture, and other hidden gems.

title: Rarh
desc: The backcountry with mixed terrains; fertile soil to the east and undulating red soil to the west. Home to temple towns, Baul music, mining and the thriving steel industry.

title: Lower Assam
desc: Home to wildlife habitats such as Manas National Park and Chakrashila; the traditional silk industry at Sualkuchi, archaeological sites like Madan Kamdev and Surya Pahar; tribal cultures of Bodo, Rabha, Garo and Hajong; rafting at several rivers; and religious sites like Hajo.

title: Central Assam
desc: Home to the historic and largest city Guwahati.

title: Upper Assam
desc: Home to the Kaziranga National Park; historical city of Rangpur in Sibsagar; and royal burial mounds at Charaideo.

title: Assam Hills
desc: Home to the historic Maibang, the scenic Haflong, the fabled Jatinga, and the hotwater spring at Umrangshu.

title: Barak Valley
desc: The Bengali-speaking enclave of Assam, home to the ancient Cachar Kingdom, and the memories of the Bengali Language Movement.

title: Imphal Valley
desc: The region where one of the earliest human settlement in Manipur emerged: Andro, where there's a sacred fireplace burning continuously for the last 2000 years, through the dedicated efforts of the natives.

title: Manipur Hills
desc: The hills surrounding the valley, home to the tribal populations in the state.

title: Jiribam
desc: The meeting point of Meitei and Assamese cultures, the sole railhead to Manipur.

title: Kochi/Old Kochi
desc: Primarily a tourist enclave. Fort Kochi forms the upper part of the district with neatly arranged colonial buildings, narrow well-paved roads, Anglo-Dutch influenced structures and large antiques shops. Mattancherry is primarily a trading city, famous for its thriving Gujarati settlement brought to the city in the 16th and 17th centuries by the spice trade.

title: Kochi/Goshree
desc: Bolgatty is where the British established a Royal Residency, which has been converted into a five-star hotel. Famous for its large golf course, horse riding tracks, marina and boatyards. Vypin is one of the most densely populated islands in the world with numerous fishing villages, tourist villages and the popular Cherai Beach.

title: Kochi/Ernakulam
desc: The heart and transport hub of Kochi with three distinct parts: the "Central Business District" (CBD) which has Mahatma Gandhi Road (MG Road) as the main arterial road along with Marine Drive and Chittoor Road; "Downtown" with upscale residential areas and the business district at SA Road and Vytilla Junction and the "Suburb" which has many business and commercial areas.

title: Kochi/Kalamassery
desc: Famous for the large Vamana Temple, the focal centre of Onam, the national festival of Kerala. Also the home of Cochin University and other educational institutes.

title: Kochi/Thrippunithura
desc: The erstwhile capital of the Kingdom of Cochin, famous for various historical palaces, museums and temples, and as a centre of the arts.

title: North Andhra
desc: The northern part of the state is home to Visakhapatnam (Vizag) and the scenic Araku Valley.

title: Central Andhra
desc: The Godavari-Krishna Delta region is home to the second-largest city Vijayawada, the cultural capital Rajahmundry, the large Kolleru Lake and the former French enclave Yanam.

title: South Andhra
desc: Part of the Coromandel Coast, the region is home to the state capital Amaravati, Vijayawada's twin city Guntur, the spiritual capital Tirupati and India's premier spaceport at Sriharikota, near the Pulicat Lake.

title: Rayalaseema
desc: The western Deccan region. Home to the pilgrimage site Srisailam atop the Eastern Ghats, as well as the ashram of Sathya Sai at Puttaparthi.

title: West Telangana
desc: The immediate region surrounding Hyderabad.

title: East Telangana
desc: The eastern fringes of Telangana.

title: North Telangana
desc: The northern fringes of Telangana.

title: Malabar
desc: Famous for its history, spices, textiles, beaches, rainforests

title: Central Kerala
desc: The central part of Kerala with cities like Kochi, Palakkad and Thrissur

title: Northern Travancore
desc: Known for its mountains and hill stations, and plantations of spices, tea and coffee

title: Central Travancore
desc: Kerala's backwaters, and the land of churches, latex and literacy

title: Southern Travancore
desc: Home to the capital city and various monuments, famous beaches, large temples, churches, and sporting events

title: Chola Nadu
desc: The fertile Kaveri River delta is the home of the ancient Chola Empire.

title: Kongu Nadu
desc: Home to the Western Ghats mountain boundary with Kerala.

title: Northern Tamil Nadu
desc: Tourist-friendly: Chennai, beaches and temples abound here.

title: Pandya Nadu
desc: Home to the southernmost point of mainland India, and the abandoned sandbar town of Dhanushkodi.

title: Southeastern Karnataka
desc: The region surrounding Bengaluru with cool climate.

title: Cauvery Basin
desc: Southern Karnataka, including Mysore. Rolling hills, large sunflower fields and Tibetan culture.

title: Central Karnataka
desc: The meeting point of North and South Karnataka.

title: Karavali
desc: Relatively unexplored region, full of empty beaches and lush green rainforest.

title: Northern Karnataka
desc: Home to the stunning religious and archeological site of Hampi. Full of other-worldly geology and nature.

title: Northwestern Karnataka
desc: Good transport connections, but interior is way off the beaten track.

title: North and Central Howrah
desc: Covers the old town of Howrah, as well as the bustling city centre.

title: Shibpur (South Howrah)
desc: Once a separate suburb, Shibpur is now a posh residential area of the city. Home to Howrah's botanical garden, engineering college and its largest shopping mall, as well as the multi-storey secretariat of the West Bengal government.

title: West Howrah
desc: A rapidly-developing industrial and residential suburban area.

title: Darjeeling (district)
desc: Hills with tea gardens, toy trains, and views of picturesque white peaks.

title: Kalimpong (district)
desc: Lesser-explored hills with unspoilt attractions.

title: Jalpaiguri (district)
desc: Home to the Gorumara National Park and the Gajoldoba birdwatching spot.

title: Alipurduar (district)
desc: Home to Buxa, Chilapata and Jaldapara forests.

title: Cooch Behar (district)
desc: Once a separate kingdom, Cooch Behar is distinct with its own language, folk culture and lifestyle.

title: Uttar Dinajpur
desc: Home to a popular bird sanctuary on the Kulik River.

title: Dakshin Dinajpur
desc: Home to a museum with numerous ancient artefacts and a Gupta-era historical site.

title: Malda (district)
desc: Historic centre of Bengal, and an important junction and entry point to North Bengal from South Bengal.

title: Murshidabad (district)
desc: Covers the former Nawab-era capital and two commercial centres along the Bhagirathi River.

title: Nadia
desc: Known for the pilgrimage sites Nabadwip and Mayapur, the royal heritage of Krishnanagar, and a major railway interchange at Ranaghat.

title: North 24 Parganas
desc: The most populous district of West Bengal.

title: South 24 Parganas
desc: Home to the Sundarbans National Park, the beach spot Bakkhali and the pilgrimage site Gangasagar.

title: Hooghly (district)
desc: Often called the "Little Europe" for its history of being colonised by different European powers. Also home to the pilgrimage sites Tarakeswar and Kamarpukur.

title: Howrah (district)
desc: Home to the twin of Kolkata, opposite the Hooghly River. Features India's largest railway complex, a colonial-era botanical garden, the Ramakrishna Mission, and the scenic views of the Rupnarayan River.
